text:
We’re thrilled to lead Tutor Intelligence’s Series B.

@tutorintel is a robotics research and deployment company that builds generally capable robot hardware. They deploy into real production environments ahead of full autonomy, using human teleoperators (“tutors”) to train the robot foundation models and make the fleet more capable over time.

To date, Tutor robots are in operation across some of the country’s largest manufacturing and logistics networks, with plans to have more than 1,000 robots under contract by the end of 2027.

Co-founders Josh Gruenstein and Alon Kosowsky are lifelong robotics enthusiasts who met as undergrads at MIT. They combine excellent research chops with a practical, ROI-driven orientation that is more typical in enterprise software.

Congrats @joshgruenstein, @KSachsAlon, and the Tutor Intelligence team!

By @RaghuRaghuram, @martin_casado, and @jamiedsully

Josh Gruenstein of Tutor Intelligence says the machine-run factory most people picture is just the top .01%, and humans still box almost everything you buy:

"Most people have this mental picture of what the industrial base or manufacturing logistics looks like in the United States... You see these Rube Goldbergian machines of levers, and you don't see any humans in those pictures, right?"

"That's the top .01% of American manufacturing logistics. What's below that? You walk into these million square foot facilities and you see a bunch of people standing around on conveyor belts or folding tables doing things by hand."

"It's kind of shocking for anybody who doesn't come from this industry and community."

"A huge amount of work, which is back-breaking work that's really hard to hire for. There's a three-month turnover where your average age of the worker doing that work is 55 years old and about to retire."

"Basically anything you ever bought that came in a box, a human had to put that in a box, which is a crazy revelation for most people... Even iPhones, you would assume it's a robot putting that packaging together. No, it's a person even at the highest level of scale."

@joshgruenstein @tutorintel

Josh Gruenstein of Tutor Intelligence says a perfect robot brain wouldn't solve robotics, because the bottleneck is building robots at scale and finding customers, not intelligence:

"There are eight billion people on Earth who all have this baseline physical intelligence that we want our robots to have."

"Imagine you had infinitely powerful software that could connect any human being on Earth to any robot and embody that robot with intelligence... Suddenly you have unlimited infinite robot intelligence... Now what?"

"The problem isn't actually solved, right? You still need to actually manufacture robots at scale... Robots are a rounding error even in the most automated industries like manufacturing and logistics."

"None of the software exists and none of the customers exist because the robots can't do any of the jobs that customers want robots to do."

"So robotics is not any one layer of the stack. It's not just about intelligence, it's not just about hardware, it's not just about the customer. It's about kind of figuring out how to put all these three pieces together."

@joshgruenstein @tutorintel

text:
同时开 5 个 Agent，人就盯不过来了

DeepSeek Harness 团队公开了一套 Super-agent 设计，思路很直接：session 别让人管了，交给系统。

你只跟同一个 Agent 说话，它在后台同时推进好几件事。

核心是两层：

Router 只负责沟通和派活，连 Bash 都不给它，用便宜的快模型

Worker 每个只做一件事，用最强的模型，但不许直接跟人说话，报错和工具日志全锁在里面，你在群里只看到 Router 整理过的结论

群里的消息先过代码规则
闲聊群直接丢掉，0 token
剩下的才交给轻量模型判断要不要管

有人在群里吐槽一个 macOS 的 bug，没 @ 它
它自己在后台复现，定位到 Electron 的 detail=2 机制，带着前后对比截图提了 PR

最有意思的是实验：

单会话 + 中立提示词，5 轮全是模型自己下场干，一个子任务都没派出去

换成强委派提示词，还是有 1 轮觉得任务小、自己干了

结果 p95 拖到 29 分钟，Super-agent 是 15.7 分钟

结论：想让模型分活，靠 Prompt 劝不住，得在架构上把它的手拿掉

代价也写得清楚：每轮 token 23.2M，单会话方案是 6.1M 和 10.8M

还有两个细节：

同一个 PR 的后续消息直接推给负责的 Worker，不再经过 Router。关掉这条直通，token 多花 37%

事件越密集越省：每分钟从 1 个涨到 40 个，单次决策反而从 6.4 秒降到 1.6 秒

大脑放在云端，你电脑上只跑一个轻量 daemon
笔记本合盖它照样盯群和 PR，第二天开机自动补跑本地测试

最大的坑还没填：它常驻、读公开群聊和外部 PR，又连着你的电脑。被 Prompt 注入一次，连着的设备都可能被接管

你敢让这样一个 Agent 常驻，还连着自己的开发机吗？

实验用的是合成负载（每轮约 300 条消息、20 个工作请求），团队自己说结果仅供参考；公开的只是部分实现的原型，不是 DeepSeek 官方产品。
完整解读：https://xiaohu.ai/article/deepseek-harness-super-agent/

You pay OpenAI $20 to $500 a month. This weekend it handed out 2 free Codex resets.
Redeem one the day before your weekly refresh and it buys you exactly one day.

That's why "Banked 2/2" got 1M views and almost nobody read the fine print.

The math OpenAI's help page implies but never says:

A reset doesn't add a week. It restarts your weekly clock. So a reset is worth the days left until your normal refresh.

→ Out of usage Tuesday, refresh due Friday: redeem now, you unlock 3 days you'd have spent locked out.
→ Out of usage Thursday, refresh due Friday: you unlock 1 day, and your next refresh moves to next Thursday.

The fine print:

→ It won't redeem unless a covered bar is under 80%. You'll see "Your usage does not need a reset right now."
→ Plus gets the 5-hour and weekly bars back. Pro 100/200/500 gets the weekly bar only.
→ "Allow your assistant to use resets" lets Codex spend one by itself at 10% left. Check that toggle.
→ No redeeming from the mobile app. Desktop, web, or /usage in the CLI.
→ Each reset has an expiry date. Expired or used by accident, support won't replace it.

The paid reset is the same deal. OpenAI's words: it "pulls your normal weekly allowance forward." You're buying next week early, not extra usage.

My take: hold both until you hit zero with 3+ days left. And turn off the auto-use toggle today.

Resets won't help in December, when ChatGPT checkout says chat and Codex start sharing one limit. What helps is fewer wasted turns: an agent that knows what "done" looks like stops burning your bar guessing. That's what our prompts are built for, link below.

Are you saving your resets for a crunch week, or burning them before they expire?

OpenAI's help article on resets: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001498-how-resets-work-in-codex

Free prompts, no signup: https://godofprompt.ai/prompt-library

Introducing Honest Thumbnails

A Chrome Extension to unslop YouTube thumbnails with stills from the video. Brings back the early 2010s vibe of Youtube where not everything was about clickbait.

While looking into how @karpathy's HackerTube works, I learnt that YouTube has a CDN that provides still frames from the following chunks ¼, ½, ¾ of each video.

So as you can imagine, it was only a matter of time until Claude turned this into a Chrome Extension. Honestly, it took me longer to make the icon than it took Claude to write the code.

Open Source and MIT. Fork it, steal it, do whatever your heart wants with it.

https://github.com/851-labs/honest-thumbnails

quoted_tweet.author: Andrej Karpathy
quoted_tweet.text:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://hackertube.org/

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name.
